name: Logitech G Pro X Superlight Wireless Gaming Mouse
description: The Logitech G Pro X Superlight is an ultra-lightweight wireless gaming mouse designed for competitive FPS play. It features a refined right-handed shape, HERO high-precision optical sensor, low-latency LIGHTSPEED wireless with a USB receiver, mechanical-feeling button switches, and a minimal two-side-button layout to keep weight down. The matte shell (often offered in white or black) omits heavy RGB in favor of battery life and reduced mass, typically around the mid-60g range depending on configuration. It is aimed at players who want fast starts, consistent tracking, and a tournament-simple control scheme rather than an MMO button deck.

reviews.content: Incredibly light — aim feels effortless after a week. Hermox sensor tracking is clean at 800 DPI. Battery lasts forever on the white Superlight.
Shape is perfect for my claw grip. Clicks are crisp. Only miss a third side button for binds.
Too minimal for MMO players. For FPS though, this is the meta for a reason. Glides like ice on a cloth pad.
Scroll wheel is loud and a bit notchy. Got used to it. Wireless is rock solid with the USB dongle.
Switched from a heavy Razer — my wrist pain dropped a lot. Weight savings are not marketing fluff.
White shell shows dirt fast. Clean weekly if you care. Performance is flagship.
Stock skates wore quicker than expected. Aftermarket dots fixed it. Mouse itself is excellent.
No RGB is a plus for me — less distraction, better battery. Pure aiming tool.
Side buttons are a tad forward for my thumb. Almost returned it; software remaps helped enough to keep.
G HUB is bloated but DPI and report rate just work. 1000Hz feels responsive in Valorant.
Coating on the white model gets glossy on the right side from sweat. Grip tape recommended.
Best wireless mouse I've used for competitive play. Zero spinouts, zero stutters in three months.
Price is steep for plastic and two buttons. You're paying for weight and sensor. Know that going in.
Left click developed double-click after 8 months. Logitech replaced it. Love the mouse, hate the QC lottery.
Travel pair with a tiny pad — whole kit fits in a hoodie pocket. Tournament ready.
Sensor lifts cleanly; no weird jitter on mousepad edges. Aim trainers finally feel consistent.
Feet scratch easily on dirty desks. Keep the pad clean. Otherwise buttery.
Came from a G Pro wired — wireless freedom is worth it. Same familiar shape.
Not for big hands; my palm overhangs. Try before buying if you're 20cm+.
Battery indicator in software is vague, but I charge maybe once every two weeks of heavy play.
Clicks feel lighter than my old DeathAdder — fewer accidental misclicks in spray control.
Dongle is easy to lose. Wish it stored in the mouse. Magnets when?
Pure FPS beast. Inventory management games feel button-starved. Buy according to genre.
Packaging is premium; mouse is lighter than expected in hand. Instant smile.
Optical switches are snappy. No debounce weirdness. Firmware updates were painless.
Right-handed only — obvious, but lefties beware. Ambiguous marketing photos online.
After a month my K/D actually ticked up. Placebo maybe, but confidence is real.
Cable for charging is short USB-A. Fine at a desk, annoying on a couch PC.
Skates + Corepad combo made it even faster. Stock is already good for most people.
No onboard profiles without software quirks. LAN cafes are annoying. Main PC: perfect.
Build creaks faintly if I squeeze hard. Doesn't affect aim. Still premium overall.
White G logo LED is subtle — love that. Less gamer-cliché than rainbow bricks.
Returned the black, kept white for visibility on dark pads. Same performance.
Motion sync / high polling feels responsive. Not magic, but refined.
Too slippery without grip tape for sweaty hands. Tape fixed it in ten minutes.
Customer support asked for videos but eventually RMA'd my click issue. Decent outcome.
Pairs with a large cloth pad beautifully. Hard pad made it feel skatey; cloth is the match.
Minimalism means fewer failure points. After a year still my main.
Scroll tilt? None. Miss it from office mice for horizontal spreadsheet jumps.
Esports branding is loud; product underneath is quietly excellent engineering.
Lightweight caused overflicks the first days. Recalibrated sensitivity and I'm hooked.
Charges while playing with cord — fine, but defeats wireless until you unplug. Plan sessions.
Compared to newer Superlight 2 hype, this still aims great and often costs less used/new.
Thumb rest area could use more texture. Minor ergonomic nit on an otherwise great shape.
Zero acceleration nonsense — 1:1 tracking for me. What I needed.
Kids borrowed it and dropped it; still tracks fine. Tough little shell.
Not an office mouse — too light and clicky for all-day docs. Gaming sessions: star.
Bought on sale; full price would sting. Performance matches the reputation either way.
Sensor loft and landing are predictable. Flick shots finally consistent night to night.
Bottom line: light, accurate, reliable wireless FPS mouse. I'd buy again in white.
